questions.question: What production role does vLLM primarily fill?
options: It trains a model from raw data.
It serves trained models by scheduling inference, managing KV state, and exposing APIs.
It guarantees that generated answers are correct.
It replaces authentication and application safety policy.
questions.explanation: vLLM is an inference and serving runtime. Training, product policy, evaluation, and gateway controls remain separate responsibilities.

questions.question: Why can continuous batching improve accelerator utilization for generation workloads?
options: Every request is forced to have the same output length.
The active batch can change between engine steps as requests finish or capacity becomes available.
The model generates an entire response in one step.
KV cache memory is disabled between steps.
questions.explanation: Iteration-level membership avoids waiting for the slowest member of a fixed batch before admitting more eligible work.

questions.question: What does max_num_batched_tokens control in the vLLM scheduler?
options: The maximum model parameter count.
The maximum number of API clients in the cluster.
The token budget processed in one scheduler iteration.
The number of model replicas created by the gateway.
questions.explanation: The iteration token budget constrains scheduled decode and prefill work. With chunked prefill, it also affects how long prompts are divided across steps.

questions.question: Which statement about PagedAttention is accurate?
options: It eliminates the KV bytes required by live tokens.
It allocates KV state in blocks so sequences do not need one contiguous worst-case reservation.
It guarantees the same throughput improvement on every model and GPU.
It stores model weights only on the CPU.
questions.explanation: Paged block allocation reduces fragmentation and supports flexible growth and sharing. Live tokens and partially filled blocks still consume memory.

questions.question: A single model replica fits on one GPU, but aggregate demand exceeds its goodput target. Which scaling move most directly adds independent request-processing capacity?
options: Increase max_model_len without measuring memory.
Add data-parallel replicas behind a load balancer.
Put every replica in one tensor-parallel group.
Disable request cancellation.
questions.explanation: Data parallelism replicates the model so independent engines can process different batches. Tensor or pipeline parallelism primarily splits one replica.

questions.question: Why is the vLLM --api-key flag insufficient as the only public security boundary?
options: It encrypts every internal distributed connection automatically.
It protects only documented API path groups, while other server endpoints may remain outside that enforcement.
It disables the OpenAI-compatible API.
It can be used only for offline inference.
questions.explanation: Official guidance recommends a firewall and reverse proxy allowlist because API-key enforcement does not cover the entire HTTP surface.

questions.question: KV usage, preemptions, queue time, and p99 TTFT all rise during long-context traffic. What is the strongest first diagnosis?
options: The live sequence workload is exceeding the stable KV and scheduling envelope.
The API schema is necessarily incompatible.
Prefix caching is guaranteed to be unsafe.
The model needs retraining before any operational action.
questions.explanation: These signals together point to memory pressure and resulting scheduler delay. Reduce or route work, then validate context and concurrency limits.

questions.question: What is the safest initial topology for a vLLM engine upgrade?
options: Replace every worker in place before running contract tests.
Run a separately isolated canary pool with bounded traffic and a warm reference rollback path.
Share the candidate and reference process so they fail together.
Judge the release only by average GPU utilization.
questions.explanation: An isolated canary bounds runtime, memory, and metric regressions to its traffic slice while preserving independent rollback capacity.
